statement: What is the sum of all the positive divisors of $28$ that are less than $28$?

choices.misconception: I only listed the divisors up to the square root of $28$, which are $1$, $2$ and $4$, and forgot their partners, so I got $7$.
I added only the prime divisors, $2 + 7 = 9$.
I listed $1$, $2$, $4$ and $7$ but forgot $14$, the partner of $2$, so I got $1 + 2 + 4 + 7 = 14$.
I left out $1$ because I did not think of it as a divisor, so I got $2 + 4 + 7 + 14 = 27$.

hints: Divisors come in pairs that multiply to $28$.
Find every pair $a \times b = 28$, then list each number once and leave out $28$ itself.

solutions.reliable: The divisors of $28$ come in pairs: $1 \times 28$, $2 \times 14$, $4 \times 7$. So the divisors less than $28$ are $1, 2, 4, 7, 14$, and their sum is $1 + 2 + 4 + 7 + 14 = 28$.
solutions.elegant: Since $28 = 2^2 \cdot 7$, the sum of all its divisors is $(1 + 2 + 4)(1 + 7) = 56$. Leaving out $28$ itself gives $56 - 28 = 28$. (A number equal to the sum of its smaller divisors is called perfect.)
